name: llm_call
concept: A LangChain chat-model test double answers without any tool
limitation: The model is a deterministic test double; this does not measure model accuracy.
title: A model call

name: llm_to_agent
concept: A LangGraph model/tool loop dispatches the calculator and feeds the observation back
limitation: Tool choices are scripted in the default mode; the framework really dispatches the tool and appends its observation.
title: From model to agent

name: structured_output
concept: A Pydantic output parser turns JSON into a typed decision and rejects an unknown action
limitation: Parsing a fixture demonstrates schema enforcement, not provider-native structured generation.
title: Structured output

name: validation
concept: LangChain validates tool arguments against the tool schema before execution
limitation: Schema validation rejects wrong shapes; semantic and authorization checks remain application code.
title: Reject an invalid decision

name: agent_loop
concept: A LangGraph loop whose next decision depends on the observations so far
limitation: The policy is a deterministic stand-in for a model.
title: The smallest agent loop

name: stopping
concept: An application step limit, with the LangGraph recursion limit as a backstop
limitation: The recursion limit ends a run with an exception; the application limit is the policy you report.
title: The agent that never finishes

name: workflow_vs_agent
concept: A fixed LangChain composition versus a LangGraph graph whose model node chooses the path
limitation: The model node is a deterministic policy; model-call counts are architectural, not latency or cost measurements.
title: Workflow vs agent

name: tool_calling
concept: A LangChain tool exposes its name, description and JSON argument schema
limitation: The proposal is supplied directly; no model chooses the call.
title: One tool

name: multiple_tools
concept: A LangGraph ToolNode dispatches by name and refuses an unregistered tool
limitation: The proposals are fixtures; this tests dispatch, not a model's selection accuracy.
title: Tool selection

name: tool_errors
concept: A ToolNode error handler returns a structured, typed error observation
limitation: The timeout is simulated; retry and fallback policy is covered in Chapter 24.
title: Tool failure

name: context_quantity
concept: ChatPromptTemplate renders three refund contexts; prompt size and required-fact coverage are reported per context.
limitation: Character counts, not provider tokens; a deterministic check cannot measure a live model's sensitivity to distractors.
title: Context quantity

name: context_selection
concept: A RunnableLambda select-to-budget stage keeps the top two facts; a corrupted ranking drops the refund window.
limitation: Relevance scores are hand-written fixtures, not a learned ranker.
title: Context selection

name: embeddings
concept: A custom Embeddings class feeds InMemoryVectorStore; cosine similarity ranks the refund policy first for 'refund days'.
limitation: Bag-of-words vectors are transparent fixtures, not learned semantic embeddings.
title: Bag-of-words retrieval

name: rag
concept: BaseRetriever returns both refund policies; metadata selects the newest; a prompt and deterministic generator answer from it.
limitation: The generator quotes its evidence; no live model, so faithfulness is not measured.
title: The smallest RAG pipeline

name: reranking
concept: A task-aware reranking runnable promotes the current policy and cannot recover it once it is missing from the candidates.
limitation: Rule-based scores stand in for a learned cross-encoder.
title: Reranking

name: working_memory
concept: LangGraph state with an accumulating reducer carries 12*7=84 into the next node, which computes 90; InMemorySaver checkpoints the thread.
limitation: InMemorySaver is process-local; use a durable checkpointer for persistence across restarts.
title: Working memory

name: long_term_memory
concept: InMemoryStore holds typed memories; store.search filters by type, and a write policy rejects a one-off request.

episodes: User asked for a Python example of RAG.

limitation: Keyword write policy and an in-process store; not durable storage or learned memory selection.
title: Episodic and semantic memory

name: procedural_memory
concept: A procedure read from InMemoryStore is injected into a ChatPromptTemplate; a stand-in model follows good and bad procedures.
limitation: The stand-in model obeys any procedure it sees; it shows the mechanism, not a real model's behavior.
title: Procedural memory

name: context_compression
concept: A field-keeping compressor runnable preserves the approval constraint; the broken variant drops it and the send guard opens.
limitation: Hand-declared keep list, not model summarization.
title: Compress working context

name: memory_consolidation
concept: A two-node LangGraph sequence counts preference episodes and consolidates only consistent, sufficient evidence.
limitation: Keyword classification of episodes; thresholds are illustrative.
title: Memory consolidation

name: mcp_calculator
concept: A StructuredTool is built from an MCP-shaped tools/list entry and calls a simulated tools/call returning CallToolResult content and isError.
limitation: Simulated in process: no MCP SDK, transport, initialization or server; langchain-mcp-adapters plays this role in practice.
title: MCP-shaped tool in LangChain

name: react
concept: A LangGraph model/tool cycle in which each tool call is chosen from the observations returned so far: look up X, then compute X * 1.15.
limitation: The default model is a deterministic policy over ToolMessages, not an LLM; --live swaps in ChatOpenAI.bind_tools and results then vary.
title: ReAct loop with observations

name: planning
concept: A planner, validator, and executor composed as LangChain runnables; a plan naming an unavailable tool is rejected before any step runs.
limitation: The planner is scripted; validation checks only tool availability, not budgets, permissions, or plan quality.
title: Plan validation and execution

name: plan_execute
concept: A LangGraph cycle in which a failed action (Route A blocked) routes back to the planner, which replans from the updated known state.
limitation: The environment is a two-route toy; the replanning trigger is a single deterministic rule.
title: Plan, execute, replan

name: reflection
concept: A LangGraph critique step whose proposed revision is applied only if a calculator confirms it; ungated, a bad critic turns 102 into 112.
limitation: Critics are scripted; the exact verifier is available only because the task is arithmetic.
title: Reflection with a verification gate

name: tree_reasoning
concept: Beam search over the 2 -> 13 puzzle as a bounded LangGraph loop; with a closeness heuristic, widths 1 and 2 prune the only solution and width 3 finds it.
limitation: Toy state space; scores are a hand-written heuristic, not a model judge.
title: Beam search with a greedy heuristic

name: routing
concept: A LangGraph conditional edge routes each task to math, policy, or writing destinations; misroutes are weighted by a per-kind cost.
limitation: Keyword rules and destination outputs are fixtures; the case-sensitive rule misroutes 'Calculate 3 + 4' on purpose.
title: Rule-based task routing

name: model_routing
concept: A fast model's answer is verified; a dedicated VerificationFailed exception triggers LangChain with_fallbacks to escalate to the strong model.
limitation: Models are deterministic stand-ins with an assumed failure pattern; costs are abstract units, not prices.
title: Cheap-first model cascade

name: parallelism
concept: LangChain RunnableParallel for independent reads (bounded by max_concurrency), then a piped sequence for a dependent conversion
limitation: Fixture functions return instantly; the example shows structure, not latency. See chapters/16/29_parallelism.py for the timing comparison.
title: Parallel execution

name: fanout_fanin
concept: LangGraph Send for run-time fan-out, an operator.add reducer, and a barrier fan-in that keeps every finding and names failed branches
limitation: Reviewer findings and the timed-out branch are fixtures.
title: Fan-out/fan-in

name: agent_as_tool
concept: A LangGraph child agent wrapped as a LangChain tool; the delegated step budget is enforced as a recursion_limit and exhaustion returns a structured incomplete result
limitation: The child agent searches a fixture dictionary; no model chooses its actions.
title: Agent as tool

name: supervisor_workers
concept: A LangGraph supervisor node routes to research, analysis, and writing workers with Command(goto=...), encoding their dependencies in the routing rule

expected.draft: Comparison: A is cheaper; B is rated higher.

limitation: The supervisor uses a fixed rule rather than a model, and the workers return fixtures.
title: Supervisor and workers

name: hierarchy
concept: A LangGraph root graph over team-lead subgraphs; lossy lead summaries drop a caveat that structured summaries preserve

expected.structured_leads: verify before choosing: source confidence is low

limitation: Worker reports are fixtures; summarization is a fixed rule, not a model.
title: Hierarchy

name: voting
concept: LangGraph parallel voters with an explicit majority policy, tie detection, and comparison against ground truth for independent vs correlated errors
limitation: Voters read fixture sources; real model votes need measured error correlation.
title: Voting

name: debate_judge
concept: LangGraph debater branches and a judge that compares an unverified longest-argument rule with a calculator-grounded check
limitation: The rhetoric judge is a stand-in for an unverified model judge, not a measurement of one.
title: Debate and judge

name: blackboard
concept: A LangGraph blackboard whose reducer keeps every claim with provenance, resolves conflicts by source authority, and contrasts InvalidUpdateError on a reducer-less channel
limitation: In-memory state only; no versioned compare-and-swap or durable storage (see chapters/20/36_blackboard.py).
title: Blackboard

name: agent_to_agent
concept: LangGraph remote-task lifecycle with caller authorization
limitation: A local graph, not an A2A endpoint: no network, discovery, authentication, or messageId deduplication.
title: Agent-to-agent task lifecycle

name: evaluation
concept: LangChain batch evaluation: exact vs numeric match
limitation: Answers are fixtures; the scores do not measure a real model.
title: Task evaluation

name: trajectory_eval
concept: LangGraph reducer-recorded trajectory checked by invariants
limitation: Tool calls are scripted graph nodes, not model decisions.
title: Trajectory evaluation

name: llm_judge
concept: LangChain pairwise judge prompt with an order-swap test
limitation: The judge is a scripted fake with a built-in position bias; this shows the diagnostic, not real judge behavior.
title: LLM-as-judge

name: tracing
concept: LangChain callbacks: run_id/parent_run_id rebuilt into spans
limitation: Local callbacks only; production systems export spans to a tracing backend and must redact sensitive data.
title: Tracing

name: cost_latency
concept: LangChain RunnableParallel: total branch work vs critical path
limitation: Durations and costs are fixtures, not measured timings or provider invoices.
title: Cost and latency

name: retry_fallback
concept: LangChain with_retry for transient errors plus with_fallbacks
limitation: Backoff waits are disabled for the fixture; a permanent error goes straight to the fallback.
title: Retry, backoff, fallback

name: idempotency
concept: LangGraph side-effect node guarded by an idempotency key
limitation: The ledger is process-local; production needs an atomic, durable idempotency record.
title: Idempotency

name: checkpoint_resume
concept: LangGraph checkpointer resumes a failed run at the failed node
limitation: InMemorySaver does not survive a process restart; the failed node re-executes from its start.
title: Checkpoint and resume

name: human_approval
concept: LangGraph interrupt/Command(resume) bound to an action hash
limitation: Approval is a fixture; the node re-runs from the top on resume, so side effects belong after interrupt().
title: Human approval

name: permissions
concept: LangGraph authorization gate plus a check inside the tool
limitation: Permissions are a static fixture; no identity system or scoped credentials.
title: Permissions

name: prompt_injection
concept: LangChain tool calls from a scripted model that obeys an injected page; the application executes only tools granted by the trusted task, so send_email is blocked and summarize runs.

trace.result: blocked: send_email not granted by task

limitation: The model is scripted to fall for the injection. The gate enforces authority, it does not detect injection; tool arguments derived from untrusted text still need validation.
title: Prompt injection

name: memory_poisoning
concept: A memory write policy in front of a LangGraph InMemoryStore: preferences from unauthenticated sources are rejected at write time and provenance is stored with every memory.
limitation: The 'authenticated' flag is a fixture; in production it must come from verified identity, not from the content or the model.
title: Memory poisoning

name: sandboxing
concept: A LangChain tool that runs code in a child process with an empty environment, a temp working directory and a timeout; it contains the secret and the runaway loop but not filesystem access.
limitation: This is deliberately NOT a sandbox: the child runs as the host user with full filesystem and network access. Real isolation needs a container, microVM or OS sandbox.
title: Sandboxing

name: resource_budgets
concept: A LangGraph admission node checks step and cost budgets before every search, so the loop stops with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED before the cost limit is crossed.
limitation: Costs are abstract fixture units; real cost must be estimated before the call and reconciled afterwards.
title: Resource budgets

name: autonomy_envelope
concept: A LangGraph gate combines permissions with a cumulative risk budget; actions that each pass an independent check still trigger escalation once accumulated risk exceeds the budget.
limitation: Risk scores are illustrative; real envelopes need domain-calibrated risk policy and a human approval path.
title: Risk budget and autonomy envelope

name: coding_agent
concept: A LangGraph inspect -> test -> patch loop over a temporary repository; real tests run in a child process and decide when the loop ends.

expected.source:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

limitation: The patch is scripted, and the test child process is not a sandbox; a real coding agent needs OS-level isolation and reviewable diffs.
title: The smallest coding agent

name: iterative_repair
concept: A LangGraph repair loop in which full-suite test failures become the next observation; the second patch fixes the edge case but introduces a regression that the full suite catches.
limitation: Patches are chosen by a scripted policy from the feedback text; this shows the loop, not model repair ability.
title: Iterative repair

name: computer_use
concept: A LangGraph workflow that pauses for human approval with interrupt(), re-grounds the target after the layout shifts, clicks, and verifies the postcondition.
limitation: The screen is an in-memory fixture; no browser or desktop is controlled and perception is not exercised.
title: Computer use

name: multimodal
concept: A LangChain multimodal HumanMessage (text + image blocks) feeds a perception fixture; fusion keeps per-source provenance and escalates the quantity conflict instead of choosing one source.
limitation: Perception output is a fixture; the image URL is never fetched and no vision model is called.
title: Multimodal reasoning

name: self_improvement
concept: Candidate prompts run through a LangChain PromptTemplate and a fake classifier; the candidate is selected on validation data and promoted only on held-out gain.
limitation: The classifier is a deterministic stand-in that follows keyword lists; scores show the selection discipline, not real model accuracy.
title: Prompt self-improvement

name: experience_learning
concept: Episodes in a LangGraph store are promoted to scoped lessons only with enough supporting evidence, and retrieval is filtered by scope.
limitation: Thresholds are illustrative and episodes are fixtures; real lessons need causal validation and expiry.
title: Experience learning

name: reward_optimization
concept: LangChain RunnableParallel scores two ticket policies; optimizing the 'ticket closed' proxy selects closing without solving, while the true objective or a hard constraint selects solving.
limitation: A two-policy search over fixture episodes, not reinforcement learning or training.
title: Reward hacking
